findings.reason: the remaining §2b node should consume `host.host_facts()` and the plan re-cite its search, instead of minting a second cgroup reader and a fresh one-shot measurement.
findings.text: the plan's §2b (plan.html:353) asks "one placed step prints /proc/self/cgroup" to settle the containment premise, but `_inside_the_job` in `reckon/host.py` already reads the process's own cgroup line as the authority for whether it sits inside a job — plan.html:340 records the same inference the reader already implements

findings.reason: the plan should name one owner of "ensure a durable shared resource exists" and extend it, or state why the reservation is a genuinely separate resource and not a thin parallel.
findings.text: `ensure_placement_reservation` and its `placement_ensure_line` restate the durable-shared-resource ensure shape already owned by `ensure_wrapper_service`/`ensure_watcher_service` at reckon/crew/runs.py:3546 (safe-to-run-twice, held-once, publish the handle), so the plan adds a second ensure surface rather than saying why the existing ensure cannot host the reservation

findings.reason: §3/§6 should extend `fleet_node.py` as the owner of the held allocation and its step placement and delete the parallel `salloc --no-shell` reservation and its second published record, rather than maintain two owners of the same job id.
findings.text: the plan's §3 design makes `placement.py` a second owner of one-allocation-plus-overlap-steps: `RESERVATION_STEP_SCHEDULER = "srun"` (:53) and its own `RESERVATION_STATE_QUERY`/`RESERVATION_REASON_QUERY` (:71-72) and `publish_reservation` (:180) fork the hold/find/publish/place path that `reckon/crew/fleet_node.py` already implements (`submit` :164, `find_allocations` :222, `placement_argv` returning `["srun","--overlap",f"--jobid={job}",*command]` :326) and `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py` already publishes (`publish_record` :305, `RECORD_NAME` :83); `placement.py` already imports `fleet_node` to *adopt* it (:514-527), which is the proof the two paths overlap

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the placement behaviour hides hold/query/publish/step behind `ensure_reservation` and `apply_backend_placement`, and §2 funnels every liveness decision into the one accessor `record_process_alive`, so the interface is smaller than what it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan's §3 makes `reckon/crew/placement.py` a second owner of allocation-holding and step-placement beside `reckon/crew/fleet_node.py`, which already holds an allocation, finds it from the queue, and places commands as `srun --overlap --jobid` steps.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's reuse_search is stale: it asserts no scheduler machinery exists (plan.html:56-57, "a search ... returns nothing"), but `reckon/crew/fleet_node.py`, `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py`, `reckon/host.py` and `reckon/nested_launch.py` now own exactly the machinery the remaining sections add, and §2b proposes a cgroup measurement `host.py` already owns.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the plan adds `reckon crew placement --ensure` and `ensure_placement_reservation` as a parallel thin layer beside the existing durable-shared-resource ensure rather than extending it, and justifies it by "mirroring" rather than by why the owner cannot host a second resource.
